Forecast from a fitted foundation model

Source: R/fit.R
predict.zuk_fit.Rd

Returns a tidymodels-conformant data frame with one row per row of new_data (same order): .pred (point), .pred_lower, .pred_upper, and one .pred_qXX column per fitted quantile level, where XX is the level as a percentage (0.1 becomes .pred_q10). Levels finer than a whole percent carry the extra digits after an underscore (0.025 becomes .pred_q02_5), so no two levels can ever map to the same column.

# S3 method for class 'zuk_fit'
predict(object, new_data, ...)

Arguments

object

A zuk_fit.

new_data

Future rows to forecast: the index (and id) columns that were used at fit time, one row per horizon to predict.

...

Unused.

Value

A data.frame of predictions row-aligned to new_data.

Examples

model <- zuk_pretrained("stub")
train <- data.frame(
  store = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 40),
  day   = rep(1:40, 2),
  sales = c(cumsum(rep(2, 40)) + 100, cumsum(rep(1, 40)) + 50)
)
fit <- zuk_fit(sales ~ ., data = train, model = model,
                index = "day", id = "store")

# One row of predictions per row of `new_data`, in that same order.
future <- data.frame(store = c("b", "a", "b"), day = c(41L, 41L, 42L))
predict(fit, new_data = future)
#>   .pred .pred_lower .pred_upper .pred_q10 .pred_q50 .pred_q90
#> 1    90    89.99988    90.00012  89.99988        90  90.00012
#> 2   180   179.99977   180.00023 179.99977       180 180.00023
#> 3    90    89.99984    90.00016  89.99984        90  90.00016

zuk_unload("stub")
